# GitHub Actions dependencies

Action versions are written as exact release tags in workflows and pinned to
commits in `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, including transitive dependencies.
The lockfile is generated by GitHub's official CLI extension; do not edit it by hand.

GitHub CLI (`gh`) is managed by `aqua/aqua.yaml`. Install the repository tools,
authenticate with GitHub, then install the extension:

```sh
aqua install
gh auth login
gh extension install github/gh-actions-lock --pin v0.4.1
```

After adding a workflow or changing an action reference, regenerate and verify
the lockfile, then commit the workflow changes and lockfile together:

```sh
gh actions-lock
gh actions-lock --verify
```

Renovate tracks release-tag pins in `gh extension install ... --pin ...` commands
in workflows and this README through a custom regex manager. It updates these
occurrences together using GitHub Releases. The existing seven-day release-age
requirement and patch/minor auto-merge policy apply; major updates require review.

The autofix workflow enables `update-actions-lock` in the shared workflow to
regenerate the lockfile after the usual fixes and submit the changes through
autofix.ci. It uses the normal lock command without `--relock`, preserving existing
locked commits.

The GHA static checks workflow verifies the lockfile on pull requests and pushes
to `main`. Dependabot updates action versions and their matching lockfile entries
together for workflows already recorded in the lockfile.

External reusable workflows (`jobs.<job>.uses`) remain pinned to full commit SHAs.
Their internal action dependencies need a lockfile in the source repository;
this repository's lockfile does not cover them.
